rationale: Banco Bradesco is one of Brazil's largest privately owned banks, with branches across the country, and most of its revenue comes from conventional retail, SME and corporate banking; it also has a large insurance arm, but that is not the main business, which fits Diversified Banks.

AXIA Energia, the former Eletrobras (same CNPJ, renamed in October 2025), is a holding whose subsidiaries run a large, mostly hydroelectric generation fleet and Brazil's largest high-voltage transmission network; it is classified as an integrated generation-and-transmission electric utility, though the hydro generation share points to Renewable Electricity (55105020) as the alternative.

Vale is mainly an iron ore and pellet miner: its Iron Solutions segment brings in roughly 80% of net operating revenue (US$38.1bn in 2024), and Energy Transition Metals (nickel, copper) are secondary, so iron ore mining puts it in GICS Steel.

cvm_sector: Emp. Adm. Part. - Máqs., Equip., Veíc. e Peças
rationale: WEG is an operating holding whose subsidiaries make electrical equipment: low- and high-voltage industrial electric motors, drives and controls (Industrial Electro-Electronic Equipment), plus generators, turbines, transformers and substations (GTD). Together these make most of its revenue and fit Heavy Electrical Equipment; the motor-heavy mix means Electrical Components & Equipment is a credible alternative.

Itaúsa is a holding company that is part of Itaú Unibanco's controlling group. Its roughly 37% stake in Itaú Unibanco, a large Brazilian bank with a national footprint, produces about 93–96% of Itaúsa's recurring earnings, so the bank is clearly the dominant business. Under GICS it is therefore classified as Diversified Banks rather than Multi-Sector Holdings.

Petrobras is a state-controlled oil company with large exploration and production operations plus big refining, transportation and marketing segments in Brazil, which matches the definition of Integrated Oil & Gas.
Suzano makes market pulp from eucalyptus (most of its revenue), plus printing & writing paper, paperboard and tissue; pulp and paper mills fall under Paper Products.

cvm_sector: Emp. Adm. Part. - Sem Setor Principal
rationale: BNDESPAR is the state-owned equity investment arm of BNDES, holding mostly non-controlling stakes in companies across many GICS sectors (Petrobras in Energy, Axia/Eletrobras and Copel in Utilities, JBS in Staples, Embraer in Industrials, Suzano in Materials, etc.) with no dominant business, which fits Multi-Sector Holdings.

cvm_sector: Emp. Adm. Part. - Serviços Transporte e Logística
rationale: Rumo S.A. (formerly ALL) is a holding company. Through its concessions it runs Brazil's largest freight rail network (Malha Norte, Paulista, Sul, Oeste and Central), and rail freight produces most of its revenue, so it fits Rail Transportation.

Itaú Unibanco Holding is the holding company of Brazil's largest private bank, running nationwide retail, SME, corporate and wholesale banking plus related financial services, which fits Diversified Banks.

company_name: SECME - COMPANHIA SECURITIZADORA DE CRÉDITOS IMOBILIÁRIOS
rationale: SECME is a real estate credit securitization company (companhia securitizadora de créditos imobiliários) that buys real estate receivables and issues CRIs, which is real estate financing activity and fits Commercial & Residential Mortgage Finance.

TOTVS is Brazil's largest developer of business management (ERP) software, sold mostly as recurring SaaS/subscription; its Gestão (management software) segment brought in about R$4.7bn of the R$5.2bn net revenue in 2024, with RD Station (marketing/sales SaaS) and the small Techfin unit making up the rest, so it fits Application Software.
Embraer designs and builds commercial and executive jets and defense and security aircraft and systems, and provides aviation services and support, so it fits Aerospace & Defense.
B3 is Brazil's stock, commodities and futures exchange; it also runs clearing, depository, OTC registration and financial data services, which is the definition of Financial Exchanges & Data.
Autopista Fluminense is a single-asset ANTT toll road concessionaire controlled by Arteris that operates BR-101/RJ from the RJ/ES border to the Rio–Niterói bridge, so it fits Highways & Railtracks.

Magazine Luiza operates a multichannel retail platform (physical stores, e-commerce and the Magalu marketplace) selling a wide range of mostly discretionary goods such as electronics, appliances, furniture and housewares, which fits Broadline Retail.

Ambev is the AB InBev-controlled Latin American brewer; beer (Brazil, LAS, Central America/Caribbean, Canada) generates the large majority of net revenue, with soft drinks a minor segment, so it fits Brewers.

Rede D'Or is Brazil's largest private hospital operator (R$28.1bn of hospital gross revenue in 2024). Revenue is roughly split with its SulAmérica health-insurance arm (~R$30bn), so the call rests on earnings and market perception, which make hospital operations the dominant business: Health Care Facilities.

cvm_sector: Emp. Adm. Part. - Sem Setor Principal
unclassified_reason: Brazilian SPAC sponsored by Alvarez & Marsal Holdings LLC, registered with CVM (Category A) in Nov 2021, still in pre-operational phase with no business combination completed and no operating activity to classify.
rationale: The company's own material fact calls it a SPAC managed by its sponsor, and CVM lists it as pre-operational, so it has no principal operating activity yet.

company_name: ARGO VI TRANSMISSAO DE ENERGIA S.A.
rationale: Argo VI (Esperanza Transmissora) is a special-purpose electricity transmission concessionaire in Rio Grande do Norte, part of the Argo group, and its revenue is regulated transmission revenue (RAP); transmission companies are classified as Electric Utilities.
